I attached our raw usage export. Happy to hop on a call if easier.

Thanks,

Ben / Karthik — forwarding Nimbus ask + our analysis. Key numbers from their export: 2,400 committed slots; 85% sustained utilization; 36-hour rolling peak days with up to +12% instantaneous headroom needed.

Options we should consider (ranked):
1) Short-term: 10% dedicated burst pool (non-committed, priced as a burst uplift) + 20% temporary tranche (60-day commitment) to cover predictable peaks.
2) Conservative: 30% temporary tranche (90 days) priced slightly lower per-GPU; gives procurement time to align.
3) Long-term: recommend increasing baseline commit by 15% with staged ramp and an automatic review at 45 days.

Operational impacts: autoscaler tuning (lower scale-out thresholds during rolling peaks), prewarming of common model variants (we can automate prewarm on cold starts), and enabling prefix caching for repeat-heavy traffic. Karthik — I need a rough per-month cost delta for option 1 vs option 3 (include burst uplift) and whether Dedicated fleet has capacity in us-west for Dec–Feb. Ben — if we go with staged tranche, what's the quickest contract amendment flow (legal + billing) you can support?

Attachments: I included their CSV in the thread; I've put a draft tranche spreadsheet in the attached file for your edits.

Thanks,
Soojin

Alex — attaching the tranche proposal and a short cost comparison as discussed. TL;DR summary tailored to your ask: 

- Immediate mitigant: enable 10% dedicated burst pool (no commit change) + enable autoscaler tuning and model prewarm flags (we will push these changes; zero downtime). Burst pool provides coverage for instantaneous spikes.
- 60-day temporary tranche: +20% of current commit for 60 days (starts on day of amendment execution). Expected queue elimination for the observed peaks and a comfortable runway for procurement to assess trend.
- Estimated cost delta (Option 1): ~$44.7k/month (includes amortized tranche + expected burst uplift). See attached spreadsheet for line-item math.
- Conversion path: if utilization remains >82% at day 45, we recommend converting to a 12-month baseline +15% commit with a 30-day notice window; we will provide a utilization dashboard snapshot at day 30 and day 45 to support procurement.

Next steps I propose:
1) Confirm you want the 60-day 20% tranche + 10% burst.
2) If yes, procurement signs the one-page staged-topup addendum (I attached a draft DocuSign link) and billing schedules the prorated invoice.
3) Karthik/ops will schedule autoscaler/prewarm changes for a low-traffic window (we recommend 1–3am PT).

If you'd like, we can run a very short joint runbook rehearsal this week (30 minutes) to walk through failover and rollback.

Thanks — happy to jump on a call to walk through the spreadsheet.
